text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday.
- The president and Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto are once again meeting Sunday to discuss the proposed tax on agriculture.
- An estimated 100 billion rupee is projected to accrue to the provincial governments in revenue from tax on agricultural income in the first year of its imposition.
- A new package which adequately takes care of the International Monetary Fund concerns is likely to convince the Fund to resume its lending to Pakistan.
- Workers at Muzaffargarh Thermal Power Station on Saturday went on strike after Chinese engineers beat 12 workers.
- Last month's 3.65 percent rupee devaluation and taxes, including general sales tax, have been blamed for an industrial slowdown.
- Research work at the National Agricultural Research Centre has come to a halt because of a recent eight percent economy cut in the current year's budget.
- Pakistan is likely to drop V.A. Jafarey, adviser to the prime minister on finance, and take Shahid Hasan Khan to Washington for talks with the IMF.
- The government is likely to cut the deficit by an extra 40 billion rupees through spending cuts and tax measures.
- The government has allowed two more firms to import gold and silver.
- The government has agreed to the imposition of taxes on agricultural income as per IMF conditions and has directed the provinces to go ahead in this regard.
- The opposition moved its accountability bill in the Senate, unopposed by the government, and it was referred to the standing committee on law.
- The government has decided to reduce development spending by 20 to 22 percent and take other measures to persuade the IMF to release the third tranche of a $600 million standby loan.
